z2m-stage-1.title: One Box Does Everything
z2m-stage-1.description: A single server handles both the app logic and the data

nodes.label: User's Browser
nodes.explanation: The user's browser or app — the client. It asks for things and shows what comes back.

nodes.label: Server (app + data)
nodes.explanation: One machine doing everything: running the app's logic AND storing its data on local disk. Simple, but compute and storage are competing for the same resources.

z2m-stage-2.title: Split Storage From Compute
z2m-stage-2.description: The database moves onto its own machine

nodes.label: User's Browser
nodes.explanation: The client sending requests to the application server.

nodes.label: App Server
nodes.explanation: Now runs only the application logic. It no longer stores data itself — it asks the database.

nodes.label: Database
nodes.explanation: A dedicated machine that does nothing but store and serve data. Because it stands alone, the app server can restart or multiply without touching the data.

z2m-stage-3.title: Turn One Server Into Many
z2m-stage-3.description: A load balancer spreads traffic across identical servers

nodes.label: User's Browser
nodes.explanation: The client. It only ever talks to the load balancer — it has no idea how many servers are behind it.

nodes.label: Load Balancer
nodes.explanation: Receives every request and forwards it to whichever server is least busy. Add or remove servers behind it without the client ever noticing.

nodes.label: Server 1
nodes.explanation: One of several identical, stateless app servers. Any of them can handle any request.

nodes.label: Server 2
nodes.explanation: A second identical server sharing the load. Statelessness is what makes it interchangeable with Server 1.

nodes.label: Server 3
nodes.explanation: Need more capacity? Adding another identical server is as easy as this.

nodes.label: Database
nodes.explanation: The shared source of truth. Because servers are stateless, all shared state (sessions, user data) lives here where every server can reach it.

z2m-stage-4.title: Stop Doing the Same Work Twice
z2m-stage-4.description: Cache, CDN, and a read replica absorb the flood of reads

nodes.label: User's Browser
nodes.explanation: The client. Static files now come from a nearby CDN; everything else still goes through the load balancer.

nodes.label: CDN
nodes.explanation: Copies static files (images, video, scripts) to servers near each user, so they load from the same city instead of across the world.

nodes.label: Load Balancer
nodes.explanation: Still spreads dynamic requests across the server pool.

nodes.label: Server 1
nodes.explanation: Before hitting the database, servers check the cache. Most reads are answered there.

nodes.label: Server 2
nodes.explanation: Another identical server, also checking the cache first.

nodes.label: Cache
nodes.explanation: Keeps hot, frequently-read data in memory. A cache hit means the database is never touched.

nodes.label: Primary DB
nodes.explanation: The source of truth, and the only place writes go. Shielded from repetitive reads by the cache and replica.

nodes.label: Read Replica
nodes.explanation: A synchronized copy that serves read queries, so heavy reads don't compete with writes on the primary.

z2m-stage-5.title: Decouple and Spread Out
z2m-stage-5.description: A queue offloads slow work; sharding splits the data across machines

nodes.label: User's Browser
nodes.explanation: The client gets an instant response even when the real work happens later in the background.

nodes.label: Load Balancer
nodes.explanation: Spreads requests across the server pool, as before.

nodes.label: App Server
nodes.explanation: Handles the fast part of a request, then drops slow jobs onto the queue and answers the user immediately.

nodes.label: App Server
nodes.explanation: Another identical app server in the pool.

nodes.label: Message Queue
nodes.explanation: Holds jobs that don't need to finish right now — emails, video encoding, reports. Absorbs spikes so they never crash the app.

nodes.label: Background Workers
nodes.explanation: Pull jobs off the queue and do the slow work asynchronously, at their own pace, out of the user's way.

nodes.label: Shard A–M
nodes.explanation: One slice of the database, holding users A through M. Small enough to fit and stay fast on one machine.

nodes.label: Shard N–Z
nodes.explanation: Another slice, holding users N through Z. Together the shards store data no single machine could hold.
